title: Temperature, salt, and seed germination
bodyMd:
Students studied germination of one seed species. A seed was scored as germinated when its root reached2mm. Each dish held20 seeds on paper moistened with10mL solution. Dishes were maintained in darkness for five days and scored once at the end. Each listed result is the mean germinated count from five dishes randomly assigned to that treatment.

Experiment1 varied temperature, using distilled water in every dish.

| Temperature (degrees C) | Mean germinated count |
|---:|---:|
|10|6|
|20|16|
|30|12|

Experiment2 held temperature at20degrees C and varied sodium chloride concentration.

| Sodium chloride concentration (g/L) | Mean germinated count |
|---:|---:|
|0|16|
|5|10|
|10|4|

Seeds came from the same mixed batch. The students did not measure the viability of ungerminated seeds or follow dishes beyond day5. The data therefore describe germination by a specified time, not necessarily permanent loss of a seed's ability to germinate.
